doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

title: Janelle Monae's encouragement and the 'Singers Meet Singers' space for kids
summary: Janelle Monae, who shares Kayla's birthday, mentors her; Dock describes a young Broadway protege and creating a live, creative space for kids, linked to her company name Fruition.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: It does. I mean we’re talking a seventh grader right now so we’re not even in high school but she’s getting lots of opportunities so far. It’s funny her birthday is the same day as Janelle Monae and so Janelle always, she’s like Aunt Janelle, so she’s always talking to her and encouraging her, and motivating her, but she has the same, Janelle is doing movies and she’s doing albums and touring and everything. And Janelle says I see myself in Kayla. It’s the same. So it’s so funny. Another story, I have another young 14-year-old who was on Broadway. I started with him he was 7 years old. And he got the part of Simba on Broadway. And so I started with him back then, he’s now 14, he played Ralph Tresvant in the bio-pick of “New Edition,” the television series that came out, and he’s also played in several different movies with major actors and actresses. And he’s doing the movies, and he has the same birthday as Janelle and my daughter. And it’s so funny, they’ve collabed and we’ve done, I talked about last night doing “Singers Meet Singers” and I was talking about it in Doc’s class today and this is my little group where I have all my singers. That’s how I met Janelle. And so we kind of just started a new one for the kids, because I have a lot of kids that are in entertainment that want to be able to get together and vibe. And so my daughter is a part of that right now. So they’re doing writing sessions, they’re doing open mic sessions, because we don’t have that available to kids. And so more like live shows and less like karaoke, so that they get the feel of performing and get the nerves and have a live band. And so I’m trying to create a creative space for kids to be able to explore and not live in their heads you know, about this entertainment and this music.
Much like the word “fruition,” that you’ve used for your business.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. That was the whole point of it all.
